title: Signal Detection Theory (d-prime) to Disentangle Monitor Sensitivity from Bias

original_idea.body:
# Signal Detection Theory (d-prime) to Disentangle Monitor Sensitivity from Bias

**Problem:** When a monitor catches more sabotage, is it more discriminating or just more trigger-happy? Accuracy conflates sensitivity with response bias.

**Direction:** Import Signal Detection Theory. Compute d-prime and criterion c from hit and false-alarm rates, rank monitors by true sensitivity independent of caution, and test whether 'be suspicious' prompt tweaks improve d-prime or merely shift criterion.

**Why it matters:** Cleanly separates real discrimination from a threshold shift, preventing illusory progress in monitor design. Trivial computation, no compute.

**Relevant context:** SDT (Green & Swets); GPT-5 system card.
